No one with a mustard seed's weight of pride enters Paradise; loving fine dress is not pride, which is rejecting the truth and despising people.
Whoever dies associating anything with Allah enters the Fire, and whoever dies without doing so enters Paradise, even if he committed adultery and theft.
An enemy who says there is no god but Allah must not be killed, as Miqdad and Usama were told; whoever takes up arms against Muslims is not of them.
Finding grain wet inside a heap, the Prophet told its owner to put it on top where people could see, saying whoever deceives is not of him.
Those who strike their cheeks, tear clothes, cry the slogans of ignorance, wail or shave their hair are not of the Prophet's people, as Abu Musa told his wife.
Told of a man who carried tales to the governor, Hudhaifa said he heard the Prophet say that a tale-bearer will not enter Paradise.
Allah will not speak to or purify some on the Day of Resurrection, such as the garment-trailer, giver who reminds, false-oath seller, old adulterer, lying king and proud poor man.
Whoever kills himself is punished by that same means; fighters who did so were of the Fire, and a man bleeding to death from a pierced boil was denied Paradise.
At Khaybar, men hailed as martyrs were in the Fire over a garment stolen from the booty, laces taken were called laces of fire, and only believers enter Paradise.
Tufail's fellow emigrant cut his finger joints in illness and died; in a dream he said Allah forgave him for emigrating, and the Prophet asked pardon for his hands too.
Allah will send a wind from Yemen, softer than silk, that causes the death of everyone with faith the weight of a grain or a speck of dust.
Hasten to good deeds before turmoil like part of a dark night, when a man is a believer by morning and an unbeliever by evening, selling faith for worldly goods.
When the verse against raising voices above the Prophet's came, loud-voiced Thabit b. Qais stayed home thinking himself of the Fire, but the Prophet said he was of Paradise.
One doing good in Islam is not held for deeds of ignorance; Islam, migration and Hajj wipe out past sins, repentant polytheists are forgiven, and Hakim kept his earlier virtues.
When the verse on not mixing faith with wrongdoing troubled the Companions, the Prophet said the wrongdoing meant is associating partners with Allah, as Luqman told his son.
A verse on accounting for hidden thoughts distressed the Companions; told to say 'we hear and obey', they did, and Allah revealed that He burdens no soul beyond capacity.
Allah forgives unspoken, unacted evil thoughts; a good intended is written as one, done as ten to seven hundred, and an evil left undone as nothing or a good.
Thoughts too grave to voice are clear faith; people and Satan will ask who created Allah, and whoever meets this should affirm faith in Allah and seek refuge.
Taking a Muslim's property by false oath, even a twig, earns Hell and Allah's anger; in disputes over land and a well without evidence, the defendant's oath decided.
A man killed defending his property from one who tries to take it is a martyr, and the attacker, if killed, is in the Fire.
A ruler who dies dishonest to his subjects, or does not strive and wish them well, is barred from Paradise, as the dying Ma'qil told Ubaidullah b. Ziyad.
Trustworthiness came down into hearts and will be lifted in sleep, leaving a mark, until a trustworthy man is rare and admired people lack a mustard seed of faith.
The Prophet said trials will be pressed onto hearts, turning them white or black; Hudhaifa told Umar this, adding that a closed door between him and them would be broken.
Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange, so good tidings to the strangers; faith will recede to Medina like a snake into its hole.
The Hour will not come while anyone on earth still says 'Allah, Allah'.
When the Muslims counted were six to seven hundred, the Prophet warned they might be tried, and later some had to pray in secret.
Sa'd urged a share for a man he called a believer; the Prophet said 'or a Muslim', giving some lest Allah throw them into the Fire, though others were dearer.
Abraham asked to see how the dead are revived so his heart might rest; the Prophet said we have more claim to doubt, and spoke of Lot and Joseph's imprisonment.
Every prophet was given a sign people believed in; the Prophet was given the revelation Allah sent him and hoped for the greatest following on the Day of Resurrection.
Any Jew or Christian who hears of the Prophet and dies without believing in what he was sent with will be among the people of the Fire.
Double reward is for one of the People of the Book accepting the Prophet, a slave true to Allah and master, and a man who frees and marries his bondswoman.
Jesus will descend as a just judge, break the cross, kill swine and abolish jizya; wealth will go unaccepted, and he will decline the Muslims' invitation to lead their prayer.
Once the sun rises in the west, or the Dajjal or the beast of the earth appears, late faith avails nothing; till then the sun prostrates nightly under the Throne.
Revelation began with true dreams and the angel in Hira commanding the Prophet to recite; Khadija reassured him, Waraqa recognised it, and after a pause came 'You who are shrouded'.
The Prophet's heart was washed with Zamzam, once as a boy; he rode al-Buraq to Jerusalem, met prophets in the heavens, and fifty daily prayers were reduced to five.
The Prophet described the looks of Moses, Jesus and Abraham from his Night Journey, pictured Moses and Jonah answering Allah in two valleys, and likened Gabriel to Dihya.
In a vision near the Ka'bah the Prophet saw Jesus son of Mary circling it, water dripping from his head, and behind him the Dajjal, blind in the right eye.
When Quraysh denied him, the Prophet was in the Hatim and Allah raised Bait-ul-Maqdis before him, so he described its features while looking at it.
Asleep, the Prophet saw himself circling the Ka'bah and saw the son of Mary, water flowing from his head, and then the Dajjal, bulky, red and blind in one eye.

Questioned by Quraysh about his Night Journey, the Prophet saw Bait-ul-Maqdis raised before him and led the prophets in prayer; at Sidrat-ul-Muntaha he received five prayers and al-Baqara's closing verses.
